record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Can we decide whether two rich words are factors of a common rich word?

evidence.quote: Can we decide whether two rich words are factors of a common rich word?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and A* the set of finite words over A. For a word w of length n, let P(w) denote the set of distinct palindromic factors of w (including the empty word). It is known that |P(w)| ≤ n + 1. A word w is called rich if |P(w)| = |w| + 1, i.e., it attains the maximum number of distinct palindromic factors. For a word w, let F(w) denote the set of all factors (contiguous subwords) of w.

It is known that there exist pairs of rich words u, v such that no rich word w satisfies {u, v} ⊆ F(w).

Problem: Provide an algorithm that, given as input two rich words u, v ∈ A*, decides whether there exists a rich word w ∈ A* such that {u, v} ⊆ F(w). Equivalently, determine whether the property "u and v are factors of a common rich word" is decidable.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been resolved positively: a 2019 result establishes that if rich words w₁, w₂ are factors of some rich word w, then they are factors of a rich word of length bounded by m·2^(k(m)+2), where m = max{|w₁|, |w₂|} and k(m) is an explicit function of m and the alphabet size. This bound yields a decision procedure (exhaustive search over rich words up to that length), settling decidability.

status_evidence.title: Construction Of A Rich Word Containing Given Two Factors
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a rich word w̄ such that {w₁,w₂}⊆F(w̄) and |w̄| is bounded by an explicit function of max{|w₁|,|w₂|} and alphabet size, yielding decidability.
status_evidence.claim: The decision problem for whether two rich words are factors of a common rich word is decidable via a computable length bound.

status_evidence.title: Rich Words Containing Two Given Factors
status_evidence.snippet: Conference paper presenting construction of a rich word containing two given rich factors when possible, with explicit bounds.
status_evidence.claim: The construction provides an algorithm to decide the question.
